<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914911_theRebbe_655" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914911_theRebbe_655__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>Joy must be accompanied by awe and humility to prevent it from leading to a sense of self and undesirable consequences.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">However, together with this it is written,</t>
    <t s="1">"Serve the L-rd with fear,"</t>
    <t s="2">except that in this same verse it continues, "and rejoice with trembling,"</t>
    <t s="3">which implies that there must be joy.</t>
    <t s="4">Rather, when joy is in a felt sense,</t>
    <t s="5">it is possible that from this one may come to a feeling of self-existence,</t>
    <t s="6">and through this to several undesirable things that branch out from it.</t>
    <t s="7">Therefore, it must be "Serve the L-rd with fear and rejoice with trembling,"</t>
    <t s="8">so that through this the joy will be</t>
    <t s="9">(not in the category of felt sensation,</t>
    <t s="10">but rather)</t>
    <t s="11">in the category of self-nullification and humility,</t>
    <t s="12">and in the language of the verse,</t>
    <t s="13">"And the humble shall add joy in the L-rd,"</t>
    <t s="14">meaning that the joy is together with or stems from humility and self-nullification</t>
    <t s="15">(as will be explained in section 6).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The Baal HaYom Huledes explains that Chava and Noach sought joy through sensation, while Sarah alone rectified the sin of the Tree of Knowledge through joy rooted in self-nullification, which brings about true ascent.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, the Baal HaYom Huledes explains in his aforementioned maamar</t>
    <t s="2">the matter of "the wife of Chava... the wife of Sarah...,"</t>
    <t s="3">that the common denominator among them is that they wanted to effect the matter of joy.</t>
    <t s="4">As our sages said regarding Chava,</t>
    <t s="5">"She squeezed a cluster of grapes and gave it to him,"</t>
    <t s="6">and regarding Noach it is written,</t>
    <t s="7">"And he planted a vineyard and drank of the wine,"</t>
    <t s="8">for wine is the matter of joy, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="9">"Wine that gladdens G-d and men."</t>
    <t s="10">However, with Chava the joy was in the category of felt sensation,</t>
    <t s="11">for regarding Chava it is written,</t>
    <t s="12">"And the woman saw that the tree was good for food and that it was a desire to the eyes," which is the matter of sensation.</t>
    <t s="13">And Noach wanted to rectify the sin of the Tree of Knowledge,</t>
    <t s="14">which is the matter of sensation,</t>
    <t s="15">through sensation,</t>
    <t s="16">and he did not succeed.</t>
    <t s="17">For "he drank of the wine" brought him</t>
    <t s="18">(not to joy in the category of self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="19">"wine that gladdens,"</t>
    <t s="20">but rather)</t>
    <t s="21">to intoxication,</t>
    <t s="22">"wine that intoxicates."</t>
    <t s="23">And although in intoxication there is an absence of sensation,</t>
    <t s="24">nevertheless, this absence of sensation is not from the aspect of humility and self-nullification, but rather from confusion of the mind</t>
    <t s="25">(and sensation).</t>
    <t s="26">And the rectification for the sin of the Tree of Knowledge</t>
    <t s="27">(the matter of sensation)</t>
    <t s="28">was accomplished specifically through Sarah,</t>
    <t s="29">[as explained in Kabbalah</t>
    <t s="30">that Sarah rectified what Chava corrupted],</t>
    <t s="31">for Sarah is the aspect of Malchus</t>
    <t s="32">[therefore she is called Sarah, from the term</t>
    <t s="33">"dominion"],</t>
    <t s="34">the matter of self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="35">and therefore specifically through her was the rectification accomplished,</t>
    <t s="36">joy that is in the category of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="37">And this is "the wife of Sarah, descending and ascending,"</t>
    <t s="38">that from the aspect of self-nullification inherent in Malchus, even when it descends below,</t>
    <t s="39">the descent</t>
    <t s="40">("descending")</t>
    <t s="41">is for the sake of the ascent</t>
    <t s="42">("and ascending"),</t>
    <t s="43">for the descent of Malchus below is in order to refine and rectify the sparks of holiness found below and to elevate them upward.</t>
    <t s="44">And likewise is the descent of</t>
    <t s="45">(Avraham and)</t>
    <t s="46">Sarah to Egypt</t>
    <t s="47">(physically),</t>
    <t s="48">which was in order that</t>
    <t s="49">the ascent from Egypt,</t>
    <t s="50">"And Avram ascended from Egypt, he and his wife,"</t>
    <t s="51">would be in a manner of "and Avram was very heavy with cattle, silver, and gold,"</t>
    <t s="52">which was accomplished through Sarah, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="53">"And He did good to Avram for her sake."</t>
    <t s="54">And through this she merited supernal life,</t>
    <t s="55">to the extent that "her life was life,"</t>
    <t s="56">meaning that the life was hers</t>
    <t s="57">(also)</t>
    <t s="58">in a felt sense,</t>
    <t s="59">for because Malchus is inherently in the category of self-nullification, therefore even its felt aspect is in the category of self-nullification.</t>
    <t s="60">And in avodah (divine service) this means,</t>
    <t s="61">that even when joy is in revelation, nevertheless it is in the category of self-nullification</t>
    <t s="62">[similar to a king who, despite being in loftiness and joy,</t>
    <t s="63">"strength and gladness are in His place,"</t>
    <t s="64">this is not in the category of self-existence].</t>
    <t s="65">And therefore, from this joy,</t>
    <t s="66">not only is it not possible that there will be undesirable consequences from it</t>
    <t s="67">(as was with Chava and Noach),</t>
    <t s="68">but on the contrary, it brings to the ultimate elevation,</t>
    <t s="69">even to the level that is analogous to the future to come,</t>
    <t s="70">and as explained in the maamar</t>
    <t s="71">(of the Baal HaYom Huledes)</t>
    <t s="72">that the matter of "her life was life" is analogous to "and we shall live before Him"</t>
    <t s="73">that will be in the future,</t>
    <t s="74">life in ultimate perfection.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The joy of the future, "then our mouth will be filled with laughter," is incomparably greater than present joy, and Sarah's son Yitzchak, meaning laughter, alludes to this future joy.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And one may connect this with the verse,</t>
    <t s="2">"Then our mouth will be filled with laughter,"</t>
    <t s="3">that in the future to come joy will be in ultimate perfection,</t>
    <t s="4">to the extent that the joy of the present,</t>
    <t s="5">even when it is in ultimate perfection</t>
    <t s="6">(as much as is possible now),</t>
    <t s="7">is incomparable to the joy and laughter that will be in the future to come,</t>
    <t s="8">"Then our mouth will be filled with laughter."</t>
    <t s="9">And although the joy of the future to come will come</t>
    <t s="10">(like all matters of the future)</t>
    <t s="11">through serving G-d with joy during the time of exile,</t>
    <t s="12">nevertheless, the reward that will come from this in the future to come</t>
    <t s="13">("then our mouth will be filled with laughter")</t>
    <t s="14">is beyond measure, even beyond any measure at all,</t>
    <t s="15">to the extent that it is above the category of reward.</t>
    <t s="16">And based on this, one can explain why the son of Sarah,</t>
    <t s="17">for whom Sarah prayed and even more so</t>
    <t s="18">(even more than Avraham Avinu),</t>
    <t s="19">was named Yitzchak, after "G-d has made laughter for me,"</t>
    <t s="20">because the matter of "her life was life"</t>
    <t s="21">(of Sarah)</t>
    <t s="22">is like "and we shall live before Him" that will be in the future</t>
    <t s="23">(as above from the maamar of the Baal HaYom Huledes),</t>
    <t s="24">and this is that Sarah's son is Yitzchak, whose meaning is laughter and joy,</t>
    <t s="25">even to the laughter and joy that is analogous to "then our mouth will be filled with laughter" of the future to come,</t>
    <t s="26">therefore in the future to come they will say to Yitzchak</t>
    <t s="27">(specifically)</t>
    <t s="28">"for you are our father."</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
